items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: he gave me a couple of weekend jobs, Friday and Saturday night, so I played a few of them

ctx.x: And let me see, I think they had a bass, I don't know, but they had a good solid sound and this is the first four-beat drummer I have ever heard. He wasn't a great drummer but the beat was four instead of one, two, one, two, that was wonderful, not what we were used to.

And I enjoyed playing that, it was easier to play. Well, anyway, he asked me to come over to the Elks and sit in, well, he said, "Bring your horn as if you're coming off a job." He rigged this all up, he was that kind of a guy. So he sees me when I'm coming in and I went for it. He sees me out there in the entrance and he tells the leader, Billy Lusdig, "I want to get this kid, I want to get him to sit in. He used to play for me."

So in those days, if you went around with a band, sitting in was something everybody did. So the end of the set was over and he called me over and I set up and played and they liked it. Lusdig liked it and they all liked it, so he wanted to know if I'd play a couple of dates and I said, "No, I got to go to school, my parents want me to go to school."
